draft.headline: Jobless claims slightly below forecast; GDP and PCE not reported
draft.summary: Weekly jobless claims came in at 194K versus a 198K forecast, a firm read on the labor market. Core PCE and advance GDP were not reported in our data, so the inflation side is unknown. NQ is down 0.94% on the day.
draft.what_it_means: Claims came in below the 198K forecast, meaning fewer people filed for unemployment benefits than economists expected — a sign of a still-solid jobs market. The prior week was revised up 1K to 195K. Our data has no history deep enough to say whether the 4K gap is a big or ordinary surprise. Firm jobs news tends to mean less urgency for the Fed to cut rates. Core PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, and advance GDP were not reported, so we cannot score them.
draft.market_reaction: NQ is 0.94% lower on the day at 29,697.75, which is 281.75 points below the prior settle and 17.00 points above the prior day's low. In the 15 minutes after the 08:30 ET release, NQ slipped 0.13% and S&P 500 futures 0.05%. The dollar is +0.09% today and the VIX 16.92, up 0.06%. What drove the wider pre-open slide is not clear from these facts.
draft.rates_read: The 2-year yield, which tracks Fed rate expectations, fell 4.2bp on the day to 4.693% and 2.7bp in the release window. The 10-year dropped 4.0bp to 5.005%, 1.9bp of it after the data. The 10y-minus-2y gap is +31bp. Falling yields usually help Nasdaq valuations, yet NQ fell, so yields were not the obvious driver.

draft.learn: Jobless claims are the weekly count of people newly filing for unemployment benefits. Fewer claims than forecast suggests companies are laying off fewer workers, which points to a firmer job market and can make the Fed less inclined to cut rates.
